_readme: Hand-written overrides for individual scene descriptions, keyed '<storyId>_<n>'. Used when the manifest's sentence-as-scene-prompt invites a bad interpretation (the model drawing a caption, book title, or multi-panel storyboard to represent an abstract action like 'shouted' or 'searched everywhere'). Only add entries here for scenes that were rejected on first generation.
l1.8s9_1: The child sits on a window seat reading a book, rain streaming down the window behind them, sky dark grey outside. The book is closed or held so its cover is not readable — a plain, blank-covered book, no title or lettering on it.
l1.8s9_2: The child stands at the window pointing excitedly at a huge rainbow outside, mouth open in delight, one single joyful expression — no speech bubble, caption, or any text anywhere in the frame. Mum is just arriving in the doorway behind them, smiling.
l1.8s1_1: The child stands by the front door in their coat and boots, holding up a single glove and looking around with a puzzled expression, the other hand empty. No basket, box, or labelled container anywhere in the scene.
l1.8s1_2: The child kneels on the floor peering under a bed, one single moment of searching in one single location — not a montage or multiple search spots in the same frame. Toys are visible under the bed but no glove.
l1.10s5_1: A busy school summer fair in a playground on a bright July day. Colourful triangular bunting is strung between poles. Around the playground are a few simple game stalls with plain striped awnings, a table laid with cakes on a patterned cloth, a face-painting corner, and cheerful families and children of many backgrounds walking about. Priya (matching her character guide) and her mum arrive hand in hand and look around happily. CRITICAL: there must be absolutely NO text of any kind anywhere in the picture. Every stall banner, awning, game sign, pool rim, poster, price card, bunting flag and label must be completely blank. Do NOT write the words "hook-a-duck", "cakes", "tombola" or any game name, stall name or caption on any stall, pool, sign or surface — leave every surface plain, smooth and wordless.
l1.10s5_2: A hook-a-duck game stall at a school summer fair. A round blue paddling pool holds several yellow plastic ducks floating on the water. Priya (matching her character guide) leans over the pool, smiling in concentration, holding a small wooden fishing rod with a string and hook, about to hook a duck. A friendly parent volunteer stands behind a small stall table with a few plain wrapped prizes. Bunting and blurred fair stalls fill the background. IMPORTANT: the stall's hanging banner and every sign, label and price must be completely blank — absolutely no words, letters or numbers anywhere in the frame.
l1.10s5_3: Priya (matching her character guide) stands beaming at a school summer fair, proudly holding up her prize: a plain box of colouring pencils and a plain sketch pad, both with completely blank covers. Her mum stands beside her smiling proudly. The blue hook-a-duck paddling pool with yellow ducks is just behind them, with bunting and fair stalls softly blurred in the background. IMPORTANT: every box, pad, banner, sign and label must be blank — absolutely no words, letters, numbers or brand names anywhere in the frame.
l1.10s7_3: A school hall rehearsal for the class play. Ollie (matching his character guide) stands on a low wooden stage wearing a simple, plain school-play costume over his own clothes, gesturing as he practises his lines with growing confidence. His teacher, a kind woman in her thirties, sits on a chair just in front of the stage watching and encouraging him. A couple of classmates sit on a bench at the side of the stage. A plainly painted castle backdrop and a red stage curtain are behind him. IMPORTANT: every backdrop, banner, poster and sign must be completely blank — absolutely no words, letters, numbers, play title or character name anywhere in the frame.
l2.1s1_3: At the end of the school day, the teacher Mr. Ellis (a tall, friendly man) hands a small notebook to the child at their desk. The child holds the open notebook and draws a small star on the first page with a pencil, smiling happily. CRITICAL: every notebook cover and page must be completely blank — no title, no name, no letters, numbers or writing of any kind anywhere in the frame. The star is a simple hand-drawn shape only, not a sticker or badge carrying any words.
l2.1s2_3: At a public library checkout desk, a friendly librarian helps a child and their mum borrow some books. The child happily holds a book whose front cover shows ONLY a simple painted picture of a fox — no title, no author name, no lettering. Two or three more books with completely plain, blank covers sit on the desk beside a library card. CRITICAL: there must be absolutely no text, letters or numbers anywhere in the frame — every book cover, spine, card, sign and label is blank and wordless.
l2.2s3_2: ONE single illustration — one complete picture filling the frame, NOT a grid, NOT multiple panels, NOT a storyboard, and with no repeated or duplicated figures. A girl sits at a table by a window, reading a handwritten letter she holds in both hands, smiling with interest. The letter's writing is only soft, illegible wavy pencil-lines suggesting handwriting. CRITICAL: there must be NO readable words, letters, names, numbers, headings or captions on the letter or anywhere else in the frame. A tiny drawn doodle of a parrot in a corner of the letter is fine as a small picture, but absolutely no text of any kind.
l2.3s8_3: Inside a small two-person tent in a garden at night, two children (a girl, Rosa, and her sibling) sit cross-legged playing a card game by the warm light of a small lantern or torch. Playing cards are spread on the tent floor between them; a packet of biscuits and torches lie nearby. They are laughing and having fun. CRITICAL: there must be NO speech bubbles, NO sound-effect words, NO captions and NO text of any kind anywhere in the frame. The playing cards show only simple blank or small picture faces, with no letters, numbers or symbols that read as words.
l2.4s6_3: In a classroom during a spelling test, a child sits at their desk writing on a lined test paper with a pencil, smiling quietly and confidently. The teacher stands at the front of the room. CRITICAL: the writing on the child's paper — and on every other child's paper — must be only faint, illegible pencil squiggle-lines. There must be NO readable words, letters or numbers anywhere in the frame, including papers, the board, and any wall posters. Every writable surface is blank or shows only wavy scribble-lines.
l2.4s6_4: A warm classroom moment: the teacher leans in beside a smiling child's desk, praising the child's returned exercise book. The open exercise book shows ONLY a simple red pen tick or a small red circle on an otherwise blank, wordless page. CRITICAL: there must be NO readable words, letters, numbers, grades or captions anywhere in the frame. Convey the praise entirely through the teacher's kind expression and gesture and the child's quiet pride — never through any written words.
l2.5s6_3: ONE single illustration. A child sits with an open notebook, interviewing people for a school project — for example listening attentively to their PE teacher and one or two older pupils in a classroom, pencil ready over the notebook. The notebook and any papers show only faint, illegible pencil squiggles. CRITICAL: there must be NO speech bubbles, NO captions, NO labels and NO readable text of any kind anywhere in the frame — no words, letters or numbers on any notebook, paper, board or wall.
l2.7s8_4: A person standing in the hallway of their home, holding an opened greeting card that has a simple hand-drawn flower on the front and is completely blank inside. Their expression is warm and quietly touched. ABSOLUTELY NO text, letters, words, captions, or lettering anywhere in the frame — the card carries no writing at all.
l2.9s2_2: A young woman sitting at a table, gently holding an old, soft-edged sheet of paper together with a small stack of birthday cards, looking at them with quiet emotion. The paper and cards show only faint, illegible wavy pen-strokes suggesting handwriting seen from a distance — never any readable letters. ABSOLUTELY NO legible text, words, captions, titles, or lettering anywhere in the frame.
l2.10s2_2: Two girls sitting together at a table, one gesturing as she talks and the other listening warmly, open notebooks in front of them. The notebook pages show only faint, illegible wavy pen-strokes standing in for handwriting — never any readable letters or words. ABSOLUTELY NO legible text, words, captions, or lettering anywhere in the frame.
l2.10s5_3: A child sitting and talking with their mother in a cosy living room, an upright piano visible in the background with an empty music stand. The child looks thoughtful and hopeful, mid-conversation. Convey the conversation through expression and gesture only. ABSOLUTELY NO speech bubbles, caption text, words, or lettering anywhere in the frame.
